transcript: I think the only word to describe how I felt coming out of the last five years is just baffled, because I don't know how you fumble such strong source material this badly. I found myself growing increasingly frustrated with this production because I don't think it had any clear idea how it wanted to portray these two timelines that are moving in opposite direction. They have this slip in the playbill, which, honestly, I think is more confusing than helpful. And if you have never seen the show or not familiar with the concept, I honestly think you will be lost the entire time. Traditionally in the show, the only time the two characters actually interact is in the next 10 minutes when they meet in the middle of the timeline. But in this production, they just kind of interact throughout, which normally is such a thrilling moment, seeing them finally come together for the first time. But in this production, it doesn't really hit at all because they. It's been interacting for the past three or four songs. The logic as to when they interact or which timeline they are actually in is horribly inconsistent. Not only is it hard to judge which timeline we're in at any given time, but it also makes those transitions feel really clunky because they'll jump from one scene to another wearing the exact same clothes with minimal set and lighting transitions. There is one lighting concept that they kind of play With where Kathy scenes are lit in these warmer red tones and Jamie scenes are lit in these cooler blue tones. But that is also wildly inconsistent and used so sparingly that it never really helps you orient yourself. And the irony here is I actually think Nick and Adrian have really good chemistry, and anytime they're interacting together, it is genuinely really compelling. And I think some of the strongest bits of the show. I genuinely did love seeing their interactions during the Shmuel song, and so I get the impulse to have them interact more in this production. I just think it's so at odds with how the show was written to be performed, and it is coming at the cost of the show having a coherent narrative that is easy for an audience to follow, because even I was confused at times, and I know the show really well. If there is one silver lining to this production is that the music itself has never sounded better. I really did love the new orchestrations for the score, and they also added this really interesting clock ticking motif that I thought was really effective. So if you are just going to hear this score sung on a Broadway stage, then I do think you might enjoy this production. But if you are going in with no knowledge of the source material or expecting any kind of coherent production, then I think you're gonna be really disappointed.
